selection.headline: AWS adds Claude Sonnet 5.5 to Bedrock and Claude Platform
selection.summary: AWS announces Claude Sonnet 5.5 availability on Amazon Bedrock and Claude Platform on AWS. The publisher positions the model for focused coding and knowledge work and outlines how to get started in Bedrock.
selection.why_it_matters: Engineering teams can evaluate this newly available model on their own well-scoped tasks rather than treating a vendor positioning statement as proof of a workload-specific improvement.
selection.evidence_limits: The frozen excerpt provides availability and publisher positioning, not benchmark results, prices, measured latency, regional coverage or verified savings. Do not invent those details or present vendor efficiency claims as independent measurements.

selection.headline: NVIDIA OpenShell puts runtime access controls around existing agents
selection.summary: NVIDIA describes OpenShell 0.1.0 as an open-source runtime for defining and enforcing which systems and data an AI agent can access. Its article describes placing controls around an existing agent without rewriting the agent, including restricting API operations and protecting credentials.
selection.why_it_matters: This separates an agent's requested behavior from the access rules enforced around it, giving builders a concrete runtime-control pattern to assess alongside their application logic.
selection.evidence_limits: Do not claim a particular attack is prevented, quote security guarantees, enumerate unsupported configuration syntax or import hardware details from the unselected safety-platform article.

selection.headline: Microsoft outlines a change-management approach for Agent Builder adoption
selection.summary: Microsoft frames scaled Agent Builder adoption as a behavior-change and change-management task, not a bespoke plan for every team. The article introduces a change-management operating model and an HCLTech customer example of a structured adoption program.
selection.why_it_matters: Knowledge-work leaders can treat adoption planning as part of deploying agents rather than assuming that making the tool available will change everyday work.
selection.evidence_limits: The frozen excerpt does not enumerate the operating model's steps or quantify HCLTech outcomes. Keep the brief at the supported operating-model level; do not reconstruct missing implementation details.

selection.headline: Microsoft's AI at Work playlist focuses on choosing and using Copilot
selection.fallback_reason: The frozen Applied packet has only one qualifying 0–24-hour article, m05, and no 24–72-hour candidate. This 79.10-hour article supplies role-oriented Copilot learning useful across knowledge-work roles. The other extended candidate, m07, is sector-specific and its excerpt is dominated by vendor positioning rather than the promised three practices. Original September 25 publication time is retained; the later metadata update is not treated as a new publication.
selection.summary: Microsoft introduces an AI at Work playlist in AI Skills Navigator, organized around practical learning for choosing and using Copilot modes. The excerpt highlights role-based use, new Copilot modes, AI FinOps basics and developments in agents.
selection.why_it_matters: A role-oriented learning resource gives knowledge workers a starting point for matching an assistant's mode to the work they actually need to perform.
selection.evidence_limits: Do not invent the playlist's three practical areas, training duration, certification, completion results or claims that this training is sufficient for safe autonomous deployment.

selection.headline: Qoder suggests turning reusable conversation experience into Skills
selection.fallback_reason: The frozen Agents packet contains no qualifying 0–72-hour article. Qoder's September 23 release notes are the only candidate marked story-ready for the required reusable Agent Skills topic, and the excerpt explicitly describes suggestions to create or update Skills from reusable conversation experience. Its 139.18-hour age is disclosed within the approved 168-hour ceiling.
selection.summary: Qoder's September 23 release notes say it can suggest creating or updating Skills after a conversation finishes, based on reusable experience. The same release describes configuring agents and bringing them into teams.
selection.why_it_matters: The reusable pattern is to identify a useful lesson from completed work and deliberately turn it into a skill that can guide later tasks, rather than losing that lesson in a single conversation.
selection.evidence_limits: The source says suggestions, not unreviewed automatic skill installation, guaranteed self-improvement or broad no-code availability. Any human-review recommendation is editorial guidance, not a claimed product enforcement feature.

selection.headline: n8n introduces agents that work alongside existing workflows
selection.fallback_reason: No qualifying 0–72-hour Agents candidate is present in the frozen packet. This 79.17-hour announcement provides a concrete agent-versus-fixed-workflow distinction and complements the required Qoder Skills story. It is more recent than the other non-Skills Agents candidate, m08, whose excerpt does not identify the five promised agent patterns.
selection.summary: n8n describes agents for open-ended or back-and-forth jobs that can be awkward to express as a fixed workflow. Its new agents sit alongside workflows, with the two designed to work together.
selection.why_it_matters: People planning an automation can distinguish a predictable sequence of steps from work that needs back-and-forth decisions, and consider where an agent should complement an existing workflow rather than replace it.
selection.evidence_limits: Do not infer a particular pricing plan, universal nontechnical usability, permission safeguards, unattended reliability or steps not described in the frozen excerpt.
